texts: On day 630 of Year 2, Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row at sundown.
A crowd of nightmoths gathered at the East Row.
Four sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.
The four sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the East Row.
The nightmoth crowd at the East Row shrank.
Each nightmoth that survived the hunt fled to the Hollows.
The four sky-cats molted during the hunt.
Feathers fell to the base of the cliff.
Nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns of the East Row.
Keepers collected the silken threads from the lanterns at dawn on day 631 of Year 2.
Hesper boiled the silken threads in sea-water in the three cauldrons on day 631 of Year 2.

q1_issues.issue: (Agent sk_attract_1 mist_light) puts the bare class symbol in a role slot for the specific definite 'The mist-light'; the instruction reserves the bare class symbol for non-specific/generic objects and requires a witness for a definite referent.

q2_gaps: definite re-mention of a mass-noun entity that was introduced as a bare kind filler ('The lanterns produced mist-light. The mist-light attracted nightmoths.'): the bare-mass object is licensed as a kind filler, but the rule that mints an existential witness for an episodic bare object is stated for plurals only, so the following definite has no witness to corefer with
review.notes: 'the lanterns of the East Row' takes Possession; the genitive test arguably favours PartOf (a row's lanterns are its members), though Possession is the licensed opaque fallback. Everything else checks out: group witnesses for episodic bare plurals, group-event + per-member distribution rules for distributive predicates, compound genus/modifier decompositions (silken exposed, mire/sky/cliff/sea not), the name-only 'Hollows', and the 'each nightmoth that survived' relative-clause rule.

issues.reason: This is the reviewer's own gap, and the calibration line governs it: the episodic-bare-object witness rule is stated for bare PLURALS only, so 'produced mist-light' correctly took the licensed bare kind filler, leaving the definite re-mention no witness to reuse - and (Agent sk_attract_1 mist_light) is true of the sentence, well-typed per a vocabulary that itself fills role slots with bare kind symbols ('grows wheat' -> (Patient e wheat)), and asserts nothing extra, whereas minting a fresh witness only at the second mention would sever the symbol reuse Coreference mandates.

gaps_confirmed: definite re-mention of a mass entity introduced as a bare kind filler ('The lanterns produced mist-light. The mist-light attracted nightmoths.') - the existential-group-witness rule for an episodic bare object is written for plurals, so a bare MASS object stays a kind symbol and the following definite has nothing individuated to corefer with; the two applicable rules (definite -> witness, coreference -> reuse the symbol) then pull opposite ways
new_gaps: a cumulative plural-subject + plural-object clause ('Keepers lit the lanterns of the East Row', 'Nightmoths left silken threads on the lanterns', 'Keepers collected the silken threads') has no licensed form: the per-member distribution rule copies the whole definite object group into each member's Skolem event, so (Implication (PartOf $x sk_keeper_1) (... (Patient (sk_light $x) sk_lantern_1) ...)) reads as 'each keeper lit every lantern' - the prompt's worked examples share only a single object ('the barrel', 'the exam'), and nothing licenses the share-out reading the text actually states

a non-Gregorian day-of-year date ('day 630 of Year 2', 'day 631 of Year 2') has no licensed term - (Day <n>) is specified as a day-of-month inside a Month/Year decomposition, and nothing says a bare day-of-year count may fill it; the parse's (Day 630)/(Day 631) is unguided improvisation (true and well-typed, so acceptable, but unguided)

a CAPITALIZED BARE plural common noun with no determiner ('Keepers lit the lanterns') is unaddressed: Names and casing fixes the singular-collective label ('the Assembly' -> common noun) and the determined plural label ('the Wrens' -> Name-only individual), but not the bare capitalized plural, which could read either as an ordinary kind plural (what the parse chose) or as a Name-bearing order/office
adjudication.notes: The parse is otherwise careful in exactly the places that usually slip: group-only treatment for the collective 'gathered' and 'shrank' with no distribution rule, the 'each nightmoth that survived the hunt' universal built as a relative-clause-premise rule whose only sk_ constant (sk_hunt_1) is top-level asserted, Name-only 'Hollows' with no GroupOf, no invented kind atom for 'Hesper', and silken exposed as a material adjective while mire/mist/night/sky/cliff/sea stay unexposed noun modifiers. 'the lanterns of the East Row' as Possession rather than PartOf is within the opaque fallback's licence, and 'in sea-water' as Instrument is covered by Instrument's substance/medium clause.
